procedural_history.originating_court: Judicial Magistrate (granted interim maintenance), Additional Civil Judge, Third, Gautam Budh Nagar (issued summons), Judicial Magistrate (Section 12 of PWDV Act)
procedural_history.impugned_order: Orders of interim maintenance as granted by the Judicial Magistrate and subsequently modified by the Additional Sessions Judge; Summons issued by the Court of learned Additional Civil Judge, Third, Gautam Budh Nagar.
procedural_history.high_court_proceedings: High Court of Allahabad: Respondent preferred Application No. 12860/2019 under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973. Matter was referred to mediation, which failed. Respondent challenged the summons before the High Court of Allahabad through Application No. 33533/2019 under Section 482 of CrPC. The High Court stayed the summons and directed expeditious disposal of application of appellant under Section 12 of PWDV Act. High Court of Delhi: Respondent preferred a Criminal Revision Petition No. 298 of 2023 and a Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 1951 of 2023, challenging the orders of interim maintenance.
procedural_history.supreme_court_posture: The appellant(s) approached the Supreme Court by way of Special Leave Petitions (SLP(Crl.) Nos-1168-1171 of 2024 and SLP(CRL.) NOS.672-675/2024). The Supreme Court allowed the appeals.

directions: These appeals are also disposed of in similar terms/directions/ observations, as above.

judicial_reasoning.core_finding: While acknowledging the respondent's legal and financial obligation to maintain his wife, the court determined that the appellant's demand for maintenance was "exceptionally high," while the amount offered by the respondent was "insufficient in the broader rubric of maintenance considerations." The court, therefore, sought to strike a balance between these two positions.
legal_tests_applied: The award of maintenance or permanent alimony should not be penal but should be for the purposes of ensuring a decent living standard for the appellant wife.
why_appellant_lost: The appellant's demand for a specific quantum of maintenance was not fully accepted because the court found that "the demand made by the appellant is exceptionally high".
why_respondent_won: The respondent successfully argued against the full amount of maintenance demanded, as the court agreed with the position that "the demand made by the appellant is exceptionally high".
policy_considerations: The purpose of maintenance or permanent alimony is not to be penal; rather, it is to ensure a decent living standard for the wife after the dissolution of the marriage.
